overview.description: German Solo is a four-player trick-taking game from the Ombre family with contract bidding, temporary partnerships, and a fixed high-trump structure built around matadors.
overview.deck: 32-card deck (A K Q J 10 9 8 7 in each suit)

history.origins: German Solo emerged as a simplified descendant of l'Hombre and Quadrille. It later persisted mainly in regional communities in the United States.
timeline: 18th to 19th century: Ombre descendants spread through Europe.
19th century: German Solo forms as a practical bidding-trick variant.
20th century onward: Survives in US local circles while fading in Germany.
history.evolution: Contract names and scoring details vary by table, but core features remain fixed: matador trumps, bid ladder, and trick contracts with or without partner calls.
history.cultural: Often taught as a heritage game linking modern partnership contracts to older Ombre mechanics.

setup.deck: 32-card stripped pack: A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7 in each suit.
setup.equipment: Score sheet or chips for bid-value settlement.
setup.dealing: Deal 8 cards to each player, commonly in a 3-2-3 or 4-2-2 pattern.

rules.objective: As bidder or bidder side, complete contract trick target; as defenders, set the contract.
rules.gameplay: Players bid once in turn with higher contracts over lower. Some contracts create a temporary partner via called ace or king; others are solo contracts. Winning bid determines trump suit and contract objective. Play 8 tricks with follow-suit required. If void in led suit, player may trump or discard. Highest trump wins trick; otherwise highest of led suit. Trick winner leads next.
keyRules: Matador order is fixed: club queen highest, then seven of trump, then spade queen, followed by remaining trump hierarchy.
Contracts form a ladder and determine target tricks, trump regime, and whether bidder plays alone or with called partner.
Each player bids at most once per hand in the common four-player form.
Settlement is by bid value transfer with optional table bonuses such as mackers and first-and-last.

strategy.basic: Count top trumps early and avoid overbidding without at least five probable tricks in solo contracts.
strategy.intermediate: When calling a partner card, choose a suit call that helps establish side-suit winners rather than only immediate trump control.
strategy.advanced: Exploit matador timing by withholding or forcing key trumps to control who reaches end-trick lead transitions.
tips: Do not treat fixed matadors as ordinary suit cards during trick evaluation.
Track remaining trumps by contract because trump count differs by selected suit.

list.emptyOverridesReason: Six-hand uses different player count and deal; overrides can be added when implementing this variant.

list.name: Macker Bonuses
list.description: Optional bonus payouts for holding first three, four, or five top matador sequence cards under contract conditions.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Optional bonus rules vary by table; add overrides when encoding specific bonus values.

list.name: First and Last
list.description: Optional payout bonus for capturing first five tricks and potentially last three under eligible contracts.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Optional first-last bonus rules vary by table; add overrides when encoding specific payout.

difficulty.easy: Uses basic follow-suit legality and weak contract selection.
difficulty.medium: Estimates contract safety from trump length and top-matador coverage.
difficulty.hard: Tracks full trump exhaustion, partner-call inference, and expected-value contract bidding.

considerations: AI must encode fixed matador ranking independent of nominal suit ordering.
Bid selection depends on both hand strength and expected defender coordination.

phases.label: Deal Cards
phases.notes: Deal eight cards to each of four players from a 32-card pack.

phases.label: Contract Bidding
phases.notes: Players bid up contract ladder; winning bidder may call partner card in relevant contracts.

phases.label: Play Tricks
phases.notes: Follow suit if possible; trick winner leads next trick.

phases.label: Settle Contract
phases.notes: Determine contract success and apply value transfer plus optional bonuses.

ante.reason: German Solo uses contract settlement, not ante betting.

deal.description: Deal eight cards to each player from the stripped 32-card pack.

reveal_market.reason: No market mechanic exists in German Solo.

buy_market.reason: No market purchase mechanic exists in German Solo.

buy_stock.reason: No stock buying mechanic exists in German Solo.

fold.reason: Players do not fold after bidding; they complete all tricks.

check.reason: No check action exists outside poker-style betting games.

call.reason: No call action exists outside poker-style betting games.

bet.reason: No per-turn betting; only pre-play contract bidding is used.

raise.reason: No per-turn betting; only pre-play contract bidding is used.

declare.description: Declare trump and any called partner card required by the winning contract.
declare.constraints: Only winning bidder may declare; called card must satisfy contract limits.

reveal_hand.reason: No showdown reveal occurs; all cards are played in tricks.

award_pot.description: Settle bid value transfer between bidder side and defenders based on contract outcome.

play_card.description: Play a legal card to current trick respecting follow-suit and trump ranking.
play_card.constraints: Must follow led suit if able; otherwise may trump or discard.

draw.reason: No draw phase exists after initial deal.

discard.reason: Cards leave play only through tricks, not dedicated discard actions.

pass.description: Pass during bidding when declining to overcall current contract.

bid.description: Submit a legal contract bid that overcalls previous highest bid.
bid.constraints: One bid opportunity per player in core four-player cycle.

meld.reason: German Solo has no meld declaration mechanic.

go_out.reason: Hand ends after fixed trick count, not when a player goes out early.

trumpConfig.trumpSuitRanking: Matador order with fixed high cards and seven of trump second.

trickConfig.leadRestrictions: Bid winner leads first trick after declarations.

notApplicableReasons.specialCards: Matadors are fixed trump ranks handled in trump and trick logic.
notApplicableReasons.shedding: German Solo is trick-contract play, not shedding.
notApplicableReasons.fishingConfig: German Solo has no capture-tableau fishing mechanics.

edgeCases.text: If contract requires calling an ace and bidder holds all aces, bidder may call a king instead.
Many tables use higher values for club-trump contracts than other trump suits.

customLogicNeeded: Contract ladder with one-bid-per-player overcall rules.
Matador trump ordering independent of nominal suit rank.
Dynamic partner assignment by called ace or king for specific contracts.

engine.deckDescription: The deck is a thirty-two-card stripped pack: four French suits with eight ranks each (Ace, King, Queen, Jack, 10, 9, 8, 7), used for solo contract play with fixed matadors above the normal trump order.
engine.suitDescription: The four French suits are Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades; each suit has eight cards and the trump suit is chosen by contract, with fixed high matadors in every trump contract.
engine.rankDescription: The rank set is Stripped_32: eight ranks per suit (A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7) with contract-specific trump hierarchy and fixed top matadors above the normal suit order in trump.
engine.dealPattern: Eight cards per player in four-hand game.

hero.title: GERMAN SOLO

hero.tagline: Bid the hand, control matadors, and land your contract.

synthesis.shortDescription: Four-player contract trick game with fixed high matadors and temporary partner calls.

prompts.human: German Solo: bid a realistic contract, remember fixed matadors, and play tricks to contract target.
prompts.ai: Game: German Solo. Use 32-card deck, run contract bidding, apply fixed matador trump hierarchy, follow suit in 8 tricks, and settle bid outcomes.

scoring.description: Contract winner side wins or loses hand value based on meeting trick target; many tables include optional macker and first-last bonuses.
scoring.winCondition: Complete your declared contract target; otherwise defenders set and collect.

nullReasons.targetScore: German Solo is commonly settled as running session accounting rather than fixed score endpoint.
nullReasons.cardValues: Scoring uses contract bid values and optional bonuses, not card point values.
